units: <cite ref="Ketubot 59b:9">Keth. 59ᵇ</cite> <he>סמוך לפִירְקָהּ</he> near her period of puberty.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 13:7:3">Y. Yeb. XIII, 13ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>עד שתגדיל ותגיע לפ׳ וכ׳</he> until she be grown up and arrive at a marriageable age and be married.
<cite ref="Taanit 16a:17">Taan. 16ᵃ</cite> <he>ופִרְקוֹ נאה</he> whose youth is becoming, expl.

<cite ref="Taanit 16b:1">ib. 16ᵇ</cite> <he>שלא יצא וכ׳</he> whose youth is of unblemished repute; <cite ref="Tosefta Chagigah 2:9">Tosef. Ḥag. II, 9</cite> <he>ופרקו טוב</he> Var. (ed. Zuck. <he>ופרק</he>).
<cite ref="Pesachim 117a:22">Pes. 117ᵃ</cite> <he>על כל פ׳ ופ׳</he> at every important epoch.
<cite ref="Pesachim 43a:22">Ib. 43ᵃ</cite> top <he>שהגיעו לפִרְקָן וכ׳</he> who have reached puberty but not the legal age (prematurely developed). Tosef.
<cite ref="Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 1:12">R. Hash. I, 12</cite> <he>פ׳ שעורים</he> the season of the barley crop; <he>פ׳ גשמים</he> the rainy season.
<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 9:9">Deut. R. s. 9</cite> <he>הגיע פרקו ליטול וכ׳</he> his (the child’s) time has come to be taken away (he is destined to die) at the age of thirty days.

<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 9:9">Ib.</cite> <he>הראה לי את פִּרְקִי</he> show me my time (when I am to die); a. fr.—Pl. <he>פְּרָקִים</he>; constr. <cite ref="Q00874"><he>פִּרְקֵי</he></cite>, <cite ref="Q00061"><he>פִּי׳</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 35a:4-7">R. Hash. 35ᵃ</cite> <he>ברכות … ושל פ׳</he> prayers for the New Year, the Day of Atonement and periodical prayers (for feasts, fasts &c.).
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 35a:7">Ib.</cite> <he>כיון … כפ׳ רמי</he> as he prayed only once in thirty days, it was to him like a periodical prayer.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shekalim 3:1">Shek. III, 1</cite> <he>בשלשה פ׳</he> at three periods of the year.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 1:1:2">Y. Shebi. I, beg. 33ᵃ</cite> <he>שני פ׳ הראשונים</he> the two beginning periods (shortly before the beginning of the Sabbatical year, and before the beginning of the new Sabbatical period); ib. III, end, 34ᵈ.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 3:1:3">Y. Shek. III, beg. 47ᵇ</cite> <he>פירקי לידה</he> the seasons when animals give birth.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 70:20">Gen. R. s. 70</cite>, a. e. <he>נשיקה של פ׳</he> the kiss on meeting after a period of separation; a. fr.
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 30b:13">R. Hash. 30ᵇ</cite> <he>מפני שחוזר וכופל את הפ׳</he> because in that case he would have to recite the same psalm again on the same day.
<cite ref="Berakhot 14a:4">Ber. 14ᵃ</cite> <he>בין פ׳ לפ׳ פוסק וכ׳</he> between one section (of the Hallel) and another he may interrupt himself, but in the middle of a section he must not do so.
Ab. VI הלומד … פ׳ אחד וכ׳ he that learns from his neighbor one chapter or one halakhah.
<cite ref="Eruvin 54b:21">Erub. 54ᵇ</cite> <he>ושנה לו משה פִּירְקוֹ</he> Moses taught him (Aaron) his lesson; <he>ושנה להם … פִּירְקָן</he> taught them their lesson; a. v. fr.—Pl. as ab.
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 2:1">Ber. II, 1</cite> <he>בפ׳ שואל וכ׳</he> between the sections (of the Sh’mʿa) one may interrupt one’s self to extend a greeting &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 2:2">Ib. 2</cite> <he>אלו הן בין הפ׳</he> these are the pauses between the sections: between the first and the second benediction (preceding the Sh’mʿa) &c.
<cite ref="Chagigah 13a:5">Ḥag. 13ᵃ</cite> <he>ראשי פ׳</he> the headings of chapters (or subjects, leading words).

<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 31a:6">R. Hash. 31ᵃ</cite> <he>מה ראה ר״ע לחלק בין הפ׳ הללו</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>ראו חכמים</he>) what reason had R. ʿA. to make a distinction between these psalms (by referring six of them to past events and the seventh to the hereafter)?; a. fr.

<cite ref="Chullin 106a">Ḥull. 106ᵃ</cite> sq. <he>נטילת ידים לחולין עד הפ׳ וכ׳</he> washing of hands for secular food must be done up to the (second) joint (of the fingers), for T’rumah to the (third) joint; <he>קידוש … עד הפ׳</he> sanctification of hands (and feet) up to the joint (of the hand); <cite ref="Arakhin 19b:42">Arakh. 19ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Tosefta Yadayim 2:1">Tosef. Yad. II, 1</cite>; <cite ref="Mishnah Yadayim 2:3">Yad. II, 3</cite>; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 8:2:10">Y. Ber. VIII, 12ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 10:4">Ḥull. X, 4</cite> <he>מן הפ׳ של ארכובה וכ׳</he> from the joint of the knee to the shoulder-blade of the forefoot.
<cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 10:4">Ib.</cite> <he>הפ׳ של לחי</he> the joint of the jawbone. Sifra Tsav, Milluim, Par. 1 <he>פ׳ האמצעי</he> the middle joint (of the thumb); a. fr.—Pl. as ab.
<cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Metsia 3:2">Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. III, 2</cite>, v. <cite ref="M01996"><he>מִסְפֶּרֶת</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 3:17">Deut. R. s. 3</cite> beg. <he>מנורה שעשויה פ׳ פ׳</he> a candlestick made of separable links (v. <cite ref="H00347"><he>חוּלְיָא</he> I</cite>).

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 43a:6">Ab. Zar. 43ᵃ</cite> <he>בין פְּרָקָיו</he>, expl. <he>בין פִּרְקֵי צואר</he> between the joints of its neck. Y. Ber. l. c. bot. (<cite ref="U00420"><he>שולחן</he></cite>) <he>של פ׳</he> a table that can be taken apart; a. fr.

senses.gloss: *load. Pl. as ab. Yalk. Lam. 1000 ושני פ׳ יש עליו וכ׳ and the camel has two loads (hanging down on its sides), one of wine, and one of vinegar (Lam. R. to I, 1 רבתי (חד מתינס 6) טעניה תרין זיקין).—[פרק אונסין, Esth. R. to I, 6, v. אינסין.]
